# job publish

## Download signatures from release: ok

## Extract changelog for this version: ok

## Verify the signatures against the app's trusted keys: skipped

## Publish the draft release: skipped

## Generate latest.json: ok

## Upload latest.json to the release: ok
gh release upload latest.json

## Publish SHA-256 checksums for the DMGs and the pkg: ok
gh release upload checksums.txt

## Update release body with changelog: ok
gh release edit v0.61.0 --notes-file /tmp/notes.txt

## Mirror the downloads to the EU bucket: ok
release-mirror.sh -manifest /tmp/latest.json 0.61.0

## Mark the release Latest: ok
gh release edit v0.61.0 --latest

  "notes": "More fixes than new things this time. The most interesting new things:\n\n- Copying thousands of small files onto a local disk got many times faster. It's always a compromise between speed and\n  data safety, but the old balance was way too conservative. Transfers are now a lot faster, and Cmdr still makes sure\n  every file is safely on the drive before it reports \"done\".\n- The Operation log got a lot more useful: if you did something silly, you can now properly review and roll back your\n  copy, move, or trash operation, in whole or in part. Even days later.\n- If a volume suddenly becomes unavailable mid-transfer (typically a NAS reboot or a router restart), the file now\n  carries on from where it was once the share is back: this applies to downloads from SMB, SFTP, NFS, S3, and WebDAV,\n  and to uploads to SMB.\n\nPlus ~50 smaller fixes and improvements.\n\n### Added\n\n- Roll back only the items you check: the Operation log is now a list of operations beside a checkbox tree of each one's\n  items, with \"Roll back selected\", \"Roll back the rest\", and a key for every action (8583f7b78, dbfcef1e8, 1f39a2bdb,\n downloads from SMB, SFTP,\n  NFS, S3, and WebDAV, and for uploads to SMB (1e7b71244, 91a062216, b354704f0, a901fb20d, 558ee26c4, 09667a936,\n  7a36d86fd, 412d46bcc, 9dd2a7d2b, dc4e59113)\n- Drop an
